lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Experience is not in newest-first order.
items.because: The 2023–2024 Westfield role appears above the 2025 Lumen role, making the chronology harder to scan.

items.says: Experience should appear before Education.
items.because: Placing Education first delays the strongest evidence of development work.

items.says: The opening bullet describes responsibility rather than a concrete action.
items.because: It does not show what you did to develop or maintain the websites.

items.says: The shared library’s value to other developers is not stated.
items.because: It does not say what improved as a result of their using it.

items.says: The editor-interview and preview-mode result should lead the entry.
items.because: It connects user research to a measurable reduction in broken pages.

items.says: The accessibility checklist does not identify the standard or checks behind it.
The method appears before the measurable result.
The 35% performance improvement does not name the metric measured.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it refers to load time, bundle size, or another measure.

items.says: The repeated “by” blurs the result and the method.
The test result is presented as an aside rather than a direct outcome.
The claim that lazy-loading the hero image cut LCP is technically unsupported.
items.because: Lazy-loading the LCP element can delay its fetch and worsen LCP.

items.says: The loading-attribute detail comes after the full result.
React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML still interprets it as HTML.
items.because: The described approach does not prevent XSS.

items.says: The XSS-prevention outcome has no stated supporting check.
items.because: The bullet does not show how the security outcome was assessed.

items.says: The long implementation clause buries the outcome and uses a dense technical expression.
The hotel-search result should lead the internship entry.
items.because: It pairs a specific load-time reduction with a booking increase in an A/B test.

items.says: The live-arrivals bullet does not say how the app obtains or presents arrival data.
items.because: The technical work behind the live-data feature is unclear.

items.says: The weekly rider count could be read as describing the stops rather than the app.
“Against 2.9s before” is an indirect way to state the baseline.
The open-source bullet does not identify a technical or release contribution.
The open-source phrase is awkwardly joined to a full clause.
The booking-flow bullet names React while the project heading names Vue.
items.because: The conflicting framework labels make it unclear which stack was used.

items.says: The booking-flow bullet does not name a concrete contribution or result.
items.because: It does not show what changed for users or how the work can be checked.

items.says: The calendar bullet should lead the hackathon entry.
items.because: It gives a clearer account of the contribution than the general booking-flow bullet.

items.says: The calendar component and its tests do not state what they enabled or verified.
The travel-search bullet does not fit the Library Room Booking entry and appears to duplicate the Lumen Travel achievement.
items.because: It attributes travel-search work to a library project while the internship describes a similar result.

items.says: The booking increase has no stated comparison or time period.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the increase is measured against or when it occurred.

items.says: The implementation detail comes before the performance and booking results.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the outcomes only after the rebuild and rendering details.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: The misspelling makes the tool harder to recognize and may raise doubts about care taken with the skills list.

items.says: Angular is listed without supporting experience in the résumé.
items.because: Readers cannot see where you used it or what work demonstrates the skill.
